Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - The originating session asked for an investigation of why the monitor button on JusPrin's Home printer card ("Launch monitor" for Bambu, "Open printer window" for print hosts), and the monitor screen it opens, don't work as Kenneth expects. The report had to cover:
     - the root cause, and whether it is a class of similar bugs;
     - expected behavior from the spec;
     - a reproduction on the real built app (Kenneth's Klipper/Moonraker at http://raspberrypi.local/, plus the fake Bambu);
     - file:line for each cause, with upstream-vs-fork attribution via `git blame` plus `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`.
   - The scope stays limited to the monitor button and screen. The printer state model belongs to another session.
   - The task was investigation only, with no edits until Kenneth agreed to a fix. The report had to be under ~500 words, in full sentences, with no invented labels, and with verified facts kept apart from inference.
   - Done: the report was delivered. Kenneth then answered the decision with **"Own window per printer"**, meaning: open each Bambu printer's monitor in its own window built on Orca's MonitorPanel, as the print-host window does. Now implementing.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17/wxWidgets). The Home page is a React page in a wxWebView; the bridge protocol is "jusprin-home-bridge" v1.
   - Orca MainFrame Notebook page `tpMonitor` (index 3) holds MonitorPanel when the *selected printer preset* is Bambu, and PrinterWebView otherwise (MainFrame.cpp:1380-1448, upstream). `jump_to_monitor(dev_id)` (MainFrame.cpp:3915) just selects that tab and calls m_monitor->select_machine.
   - Orca has one DeviceManager selected machine and one printer agent at a time. The agent is chosen by the selected preset (GUI_App::switch_printer_agent, GUI_App.cpp:3573): BBL/fake for Bambu, "orca" otherwise. Verified: after switching to the Klipper preset, the fake Bambu got no more updates.
   - MonitorPanel always shows `dev->get_selected_machine()`. Its `Show(bool)` override starts and stops its update timer. `select_machine()` queues wxEVT_COMMAND_CHOICE_SELECTED to on_select_printer → set_selected_machine.
   - Upstream DevManager::set_selected_machine disconnects and reconnects a LAN machine that is already selected (DevManager.cpp:519-530). The fake answers that disconnect with "lost", and GUI_App.cpp:2112 then selects "".
   - Upstream code reaches `wxGetApp().mainframe->m_monitor` directly in several places, so a second instance won't receive those calls (known limitation):
     - StatusPanel.cpp:2190-2236 lays out the main panel;
     - HMSPanel.cpp:124 posts EVT_ALREADY_READ_HMS to the main panel;
     - DeviceErrorDialog.cpp:391 and :421 jump the main window;
     - CalibrationWizardCaliPage.cpp:196;
     - MultiMachineManagerPage.cpp:24.
   - StatusPanel creates a WebView (StatusPanel.cpp:1532), so destroying the window needs PrinterWindow's deferred release (`is_adding_script_handler`).
   - Home card's "Online" rests on `has_recent_printer_data` (PrinterDiscovery.cpp:69, 30 s), so the Bambu button disappears within 30 s of the agent swap.
   - Fork stewardship: no upstream file edits; Orca surfaces stay in the Notebook; the shell never edits the page list. A change to upstream files needs a merge-tree simulation. This change touches only fork files.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **Spec**
     - `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md` 3.1/3.4: Monitor is a pop-out surface (camera, progress, state, temps, alerts, Pause/Resume/Stop).
     - Canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ: comp-printer-card shows "Launch monitor" only on expandedPrinting (Bambu X1 Carbon); main-02-printer-popover-overlay has a monitor glyph on every row, the offline Voron included. There is no Monitor screen board.
   - **Home page**
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx:156-170`: the button is shown when `canLaunchMonitor`, labelled by `connectionKind==='host'`.
     - `App.tsx:307` sends `launch_monitor {id}`; `HomeHost.cpp:213` receives it.
   - **`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`**
     - Gates: `describe_device` (line ~147) sets `can_launch_monitor = connected`. The named-printer loop (lines 340-365) sets it true when print_host is saved, and false when Moonraker is Unreachable or still checking.
     - EDITED: `launch_monitor` now ends with `open_monitor_window(device_id);` instead of `m_frame.jump_to_monitor(device_id)`. Added:
       ```cpp
       void OrcaHomeBackend::open_monitor_window(const std::string& device_id)
       {
           // One window, since Orca monitors one machine at a time; showing another
           // printer moves it there.
           if (!m_monitor_window || m_monitor_window->closing())
               m_monitor_window = new MonitorWindow();
           m_monitor_window->show_printer(device_id);
       }
       ```
     - EDITED: the destructor also calls `if (m_monitor_window) m_monitor_window->close();`. `m_frame` is still used elsewhere (lines 527, 554, 585…).
   - **`OrcaHomeBackend.hpp`** — EDITED:
     - added `#include "MonitorWindow.hpp"`;
     - added a public `void open_monitor_window(const std::string& device_id);` with a comment ("A Bambu Lab printer's monitor in a window of its own, showing the device `device_id`; the header's printer menu opens it too.");
     - added the member `wxWeakRef<MonitorWindow> m_monitor_window;`.
   - **NEW `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/PopOutWindow.hpp/.cpp`**: a base wxFrame (no parent).
     - Interface: `close()`, `closing()`, `bring_forward()` (Iconize(false); Raise()), protected ctor `PopOutWindow(const wxString& title)` (sets main-frame icons, binds close→close() and the release timer), and `set_content(wxWindow*)` (sizer, FromDIP 1200x800, CentreOnScreen, UpdateFrameDarkUI).
     - Private `release()`: if `is_adding_script_handler()`, Hide and retry in 50 ms; otherwise Destroy the content, then Destroy the frame. The long macOS comment was moved from PrinterWindow.
   - **`PrinterWindow.hpp/.cpp`** — EDITED: now `class PrinterWindow final : public PopOutWindow`.
     - Keeps `view()` and `page_url()`. Removed the release/timer/closing members and includes.
     - Ctor: `PopOutWindow(name)`; `m_view = new PrinterWebView(this); set_content(m_view); Show(); load_url(...)`.
     - The harness at tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:5409-5480 uses `printer_windows()`, `view()`, `closing()` and `Close()`, all still available.
   - **NEW `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/MonitorWindow.hpp`**:
     - `class MonitorWindow final : public PopOutWindow` with `MonitorWindow()`, `void show_printer(const std::string& device_id)`, `MonitorPanel* panel() const`.
     - Private `update_title()`, `MonitorPanel* m_panel`, `wxTimer m_title_timer`, `std::string m_titled_device`.
     - The header comment explains: a second MonitorPanel instance; the Notebook page follows the selected profile; one window because there is one selected machine and agent; while the project printer isn't Bambu, the monitor says so in its own words.
   - **NEW `MonitorWindow.cpp`**:
     ```cpp
     MonitorWindow::MonitorWindow() : PopOutWindow(wxString()), m_title_timer(this)
     {
         m_panel = new MonitorPanel(this, wxID_ANY);
         set_content(m_panel);
         Show();
         m_panel->Show(true);   // a frame doesn't call the page's Show()
         Bind(wxEVT_TIMER, [this](wxTimerEvent&) { update_title(); }, m_title_timer.GetId());
         m_title_timer.Start(kTitleRefreshMs); // 1000
     }
     void MonitorWindow::show_printer(const std::string& device_id)
     {
         if (const MachineObject* shown = selected_machine(); shown == nullptr || shown->get_dev_id() != device_id)
             m_panel->select_machine(device_id);   // avoid upstream's needless LAN reconnect
         CallAfter([this] { update_title(); });   // selection is queued
         bring_forward();
     }
     void MonitorWindow::update_title()  // title = named printer linked to the selected dev id, else get_dev_name()
     ```
     Includes: DeviceCore/DevManager.h, DeviceManager.hpp, GUI_App.hpp, JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.hpp, Monitor.hpp.
   - **Not yet edited**
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` (Home list lines 88-102): must add PopOutWindow.cpp/.hpp and MonitorWindow.cpp/.hpp. The build's baked GIT_COMMIT_HASH is e27c962864, equal to HEAD, so a CMake rerun won't recompile everything. Don't commit between the edit and the build.
     - The top-bar chip still uses `SetupCommands::open_monitor()` (SetupCommands.cpp:600-604: `frame->select_tab(tpMonitor)`), invoked from PrinterMenu.cpp:125. `printer_connection()` (SetupCommands.cpp:272-295) uses `get_selected_machine()`. Planned:
       - PrinterMenu's invoke opens `installed_shell()->home_view()->backend().open_monitor_window(device)`, where device is the named printer's device_id if linked, otherwise the selected machine's id;
       - a small SetupCommands helper picks that device;
       - remove or replace `open_monitor()`.
       `home_view()` is at ShellController.hpp:89 and `backend()` returns `OrcaHomeBackend&` (HomeWebView.hpp:53).
   - **Notes written**: `/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_06a35cc1-bf6c-485d-bf62-19ee49343bbe/monitor-button-investigation.md`.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - The first scratch app hung at the splash screen in `MainFrame::FileHistory::LoadThumbnails`. Fixed by emptying `recent`/`recent_projects` in the scratch conf.
   - An `rm -rf $R/data/log/*` was blocked by a safety check after a `cd`. I didn't retry; used absolute paths without removal.
   - computer-use `request_access` for `io.jusprin.monitor-investigation` was denied twice, and `screencapture -l` fails (no screen-recording permission). The workaround:
     - an instrumented Home page at `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8737/index.html` (inject.js logs envelopes and runs queued commands from `run/cmdq/*.json`: `{"click":sel,"text":..}`, `{"snap":1}`, `{"type":..,"payload":..}`);
     - server.py on port 8737 writing `events.jsonl`;
     - a Swift `wins` tool listing window bounds;
     - lldb: `expr -l c++ -- ((Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxAppConsoleBase::ms_appInstance)->mainframe->m_tabpanel->GetSelection()` (`wxTheApp` is undeclared in lldb).
   - A later page click returned found:false. Worked around by sending the same `launch_monitor` message directly.
   - The zsh glob `--include=*.cpp` failed. Used plain grep without `--include`.

5. Problem Solving (investigation results, verified on the real build e27c962864 using a scratch copy at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/ee181d60-9c47-47c1-b71d-f5bedc8844da/scratchpad/run/`):
   - **Scratch setup**: `JusPrinMon.app` with bundle id `io.jusprin.monitor-investigation`, and a data folder copied from Kenneth's with these changes:
     - added a "Klipper Pi" preset (inherits MyKlipper 0.4 nozzle, moonraker, http://raspberrypi.local);
     - fake_printer true, FAKE001 linked to "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", local_machines cleared.
   - **Bambu card**: the main window swaps Home for Orca's Device page (MonitorPanel), with the project header on top. It is not a pop-out.
   - **Klipper card**: a separate 1200x800 PrinterWindow opens on Mainsail. The card says "Connected" and offers the button while Klipper is shut down.
   - **Bambu card with the Klipper preset selected**: page 3 holds the Klipper's PrinterWebView, so the Klipper page appears instead of the Bambu monitor.
   - **Root cause**: fork code `OrcaHomeBackend::launch_monitor` calls upstream `jump_to_monitor` (fork commits c11c8d3cb1 and cc017e0b22), whose page belongs to the selected preset (upstream). The print-host path avoided this with PrinterWindow (4e3a78cc89). The chip (67361926b0) has the same class of problem.
   - **Side observations**:
     - the fake's reconnect leads to the monitor showing no printer (real plug-in behaviour unknown);
     - selecting the Klipper preset adds a duplicate "raspberrypi.local · Not connected" card.
   - The scratch app (pid 87124) and server were stopped.

6. All user messages:
   - The initial task (from the originating session): "Investigate why the monitor button on JusPrin's Home printer card, and the monitor screen it opens, don't work as Kenneth expects. Find the root cause, and say whether it belongs to a class of similar bugs. Don't just patch one symptom." It included the steps and these rules: "This is investigation only. Make no code edits, and don't commit, until you have reported the root cause and Kenneth has agreed to a fix." "Follow AGENTS.md's shared-machine build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, use `-j4`, and reuse the existing `build/arm64`." "Write the report the way `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` asks: full sentences, no labels you made up, outcomes not the journey, under about 500 words, with verified facts kept apart from inference." It also said to use an isolated `--datadir`, never drive another running JusPrin instance, and keep to the monitor button and screen (the state model belongs to another session).
   - Kenneth's reply: "Own window per printer".

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Add PopOutWindow.{hpp,cpp} and MonitorWindow.{hpp,cpp} to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after PrinterWindow.
   - Route the header chip's monitor entry (PrinterMenu.cpp:125) to `open_monitor_window`, with the device from the named link or else the selected machine. Replace or remove `SetupCommands::open_monitor`.
   - Optionally add a shell-harness check (near shell_harness.cpp:6331, the fake Bambu card test) that `launch_monitor` opens one MonitorWindow, leaves the Notebook selection unchanged, and selects the device.
   - Build: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, then `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target OrcaSlicer -- -j4` (decide all targets up front; run in its own process group; run in the background).
   - Test before and after on the real app with the scratch setup:
     - the Bambu card opens a separate window whose title is the printer name, and the Notebook selection stays on Home;
     - with the Klipper preset selected, no Klipper page shows;
     - the Klipper window still works;
     - quick close/reopen works;
     - the chip entry works.
   - The visual layout can't be screenshotted, so say so.
   - Report the outcome under ~500 words, including limitations:
     - one Bambu monitor at a time;
     - it only works while the project's printer is Bambu;
     - upstream calls to mainframe->m_monitor (layout, HMS read tag, error-dialog jumps) still target the hidden main panel.
   - Do not commit unless asked. Never stage the other sessions' doc changes (agent-docs/jusprin/README.md, mcp-tool-extension-guide.md, connection-skill-guide.md).

8. Current Work:
   I had just edited OrcaHomeBackend.cpp/.hpp to use the new MonitorWindow. The last command checked the remaining `m_frame` uses in OrcaHomeBackend.cpp, which are still needed (MessageDialog parents, select_tab at 585/596, import_model at 605). The plan list was at step 2 or 3 ("Implement window and route the card button"). Next was the sources.cmake edit and the chip routing.

9. Optional Next Step:
   Continue implementing Kenneth's choice, "Own window per printer":
   - Add the four new files to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` beside `GUI/JusPrin/Home/PrinterWindow.cpp`.
   - Change the header printer menu's monitor row (PrinterMenu.cpp:125, `machine.invoke = [] { SetupCommands::open_monitor(); };`) to open the same window via `installed_shell()->home_view()->backend().open_monitor_window(device_id)`.

content.text:
The monitor button on a Bambu printer's Home card now opens that printer's monitor in its own window. The main window stays on whatever page the person was on. I built and tested it on a scratch copy of the app with the fake Bambu printer; nothing is committed yet.

**What was wrong.** The card's button switched the main window to Orca's Device page. Which view fills that page depends on the printer selected for the project, not on the card that was clicked. So the button replaced Home instead of opening a pop-out. And when the project's printer was the Klipper printer, it showed the Klipper web page instead of the Bambu monitor.

**What I changed** (all in JusPrin's own files; no OrcaSlicer files edited):
- **New window:** a separate window holds a second copy of Orca's own Bambu monitor panel. Its title is the printer's name. It opens wide enough to show every column without a horizontal scrollbar, capped at the screen size.
- **Header menu:** the printer menu's monitor row in the header now opens the same window. Before, it switched the main window's page too.
- **Shared window code:** the Klipper printer window and the new window now share one base class. It covers the icon, sizing, and the delayed safe close that the macOS web views need.
- **No reconnect for nothing:** asking for a printer the monitor already shows no longer makes Orca disconnect and reconnect it.

**What I tested and saw:**
- **Card button:** clicking it on the real Home page opened one window titled "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", showing the fake printer's live temperatures. The main window stayed on Home.
- **Second click:** it brought back the same window rather than opening another.
- **Klipper window:** it still opens.
- **Close and reopen:** I closed the monitor and asked for it again at the same moment, three times. Each time the app kept running with exactly one monitor window.
- **Quitting:** quitting by closing the main window, with both pop-outs open, exited cleanly.
- **Klipper profile selected:** the window still shows the Bambu monitor, not the Klipper page. That monitor reads "Failed to connect to the printer", because Orca only talks to Bambu printers while a Bambu profile is selected.

**Not verified or still limited:**
- **Header menu click:** I couldn't click the header menu row, because I have no screen control on this Mac. I checked that it would pick the fake printer, but the click itself is untested.
- **One printer at a time:** there is only one Bambu monitor window, because Orca follows one Bambu printer at a time.
- **Upstream calls:** some of Orca's own code still talks to the monitor inside the main window, so it misses the new window. That covers a layout refresh, marking assistant messages as read, and the jumps from error dialogs.
- **Card availability:** while the project's printer isn't Bambu, the Bambu card hides its button within about 30 seconds, as before.
- **Automated test:** I didn't add a test to the shell test harness for this.

content.text:
I've sent you eight screenshots of the new monitor window. They come from a scratch copy of JusPrin with its own data folder and the fake Bambu printer, plus your real Klipper Pi. Most of them show the change working. Screenshot 6 shows a problem I found while taking them.

1. **Before the click:** Home, with the Bambu card expanded to show "Launch monitor".
2. **After the click:** the monitor opens in its own window, titled "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2". It shows the fake printer's live temperatures, and every column fits without a scrollbar.
3. **Home stays put:** the main window is still on Home behind the monitor. Before this change, the click replaced Home with Orca's Device page.
4. **Header menu:** this is the printer menu in the header of an open project. Its first row, with the monitor icon, is the entry I changed.
5. **Menu row clicked:** that row opens the same monitor window over the project. This is the click I couldn't test earlier. It now works.
6. **The problem:** I switched the project's printer to Klipper Pi while the monitor window was open. Orca then picks the Klipper host as its one followed machine. The window follows it, renames itself "raspberrypi.local", and shows Bambu-only controls with "Connecting…" for a printer that isn't a Bambu printer.
7. **Klipper window:** opening the Klipper card's printer window after my refactor still shows Mainsail. It reports Klipper as shut down.
8. **Monitor while Klipper is selected:** clicking "Launch monitor" on the Bambu card in that state opens the Bambu monitor stuck on "Connecting…". The card still offers the button for up to 30 seconds after the switch.

Screenshots 2 and 5 also show an empty strip below the monitor's content. Orca's own monitor panel doesn't stretch to fill the window's height.

The screenshots are in `monitor-window-screenshots/` at the top of the repository. That folder is untracked, so you can delete it when you're done.

**Decision needed:** what should the Bambu monitor window do when the project's printer changes to one that isn't a Bambu printer? This is your call because it's what a person sees mid-task. The root of it: Orca talks to only one kind of printer at a time, chosen by the project's printer, so the monitor can't keep showing the Bambu printer after the switch.
- **Close it:** close the window when the switch happens. This is the smallest change. The cost is that the window disappears without saying why.
- **Show a message:** keep the window open, and replace its contents with a sentence saying the monitor works only while the project's printer is this Bambu printer, plus a button to switch back. That's clearer for the person, but it's more code and needs wording.
- **Leave it:** no work, but people see screenshot 6.

My pick is to close it now and add the message later if it turns out people miss the window. Which do you want?

input.ask: Bind the window to its printer now, then prototype the separate connection?

content.text:
Yes, that answers it, and you're right that I misread the relationship. You want the monitor window to belong to its printer. It stays until the person closes it or quits the app, whatever happens in the main window. I built it as a second view of the one printer Orca is connected to at the moment, and that printer follows the project's printer in the main window. That's why switching the project to Klipper Pi turned the Bambu window into a "raspberrypi.local" window.

**Why it isn't a one-line fix.** I checked the code. Everything below is upstream OrcaSlicer behaviour, confirmed with `git blame` against the upstream branches:

- **One printer agent.** Orca keeps one printer agent (its connection layer) at a time, chosen by the project's printer profile (`GUI_App.cpp:3573`). When someone picks a non-Bambu profile, `Tab.cpp:2118` swaps the agent, and the swap disconnects the Bambu printer (`NetworkAgent.cpp:116-132`). JusPrin's own printer-switch path calls the same swap (`ShellController.cpp:1537`).
- **One connected Bambu printer.** Orca keeps one selected Bambu printer, and selecting another one disconnects the first (`DevManager.cpp:480-500`). Sending a print to a different Bambu printer from the main window selects that printer, so it would take the connection away from an open monitor window.
- **One LAN connection in Bambu's plug-in.** Bambu's network plug-in seems to allow one local-network printer connection at a time. This is my reading of its interface, not tested: its disconnect call takes no printer, and the plug-in holds a single agent (`BBLNetworkPlugin.cpp:250`). If that's right, two Bambu printers on the local network can't both be live in their own windows.

**Decision needed:** how far should the monitor window's independence go? Your rule decides what it must do, but meeting it fully means changing OrcaSlicer's own files, and every changed line there is re-resolved at each rebase. The options:

- **Bind the window to its printer.** It never shows a different printer, and it closes only when the person or the app closes it. While Orca can't reach the printer, it says so in plain words instead of showing another machine. This change is small and touches only JusPrin's files. But the window goes quiet whenever the project's printer isn't that Bambu printer.
- **Also keep the Bambu connection alive.** This keeps the Bambu printer connected next to the project printer's connection while its window is open. It changes Orca's connection layer and machine selection in several OrcaSlicer files. It's probably days of work, and I haven't measured it. Even then, only one Bambu local-network printer can be live at a time if my reading of the plug-in is right.
- **Talk to Bambu printers directly.** JusPrin would run its own connection to Bambu printers and bypass the plug-in. I haven't investigated this, and I'd want to research Bambu's current rules on third-party local access before recommending it.

My pick: bind the window to its printer now, since that's needed either way. Then build a rough prototype of keeping the Bambu connection alive, so you can decide on it with its real cost and limits in hand. Do you want me to do both, or only bind the window for now?
